answer: The nectar holds work receipts rather than names, so the velvet of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. Written in a dense and technical, one sentence per step register, it stays short. What survives to the beacon is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. The design leans on bond keyed to a hardware root, split across independent auditors, duplicates are caught by replay, not by name. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work.
